chunks: The sentence is surely justified against most of them, for they do not believe.

key_terms.حَقَّ الْقَوْلُ: The sentence/decreed word has become due/justified

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that the 'word has been justified' against those who do not believe?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as indicating that the 'divine word' (Qawl) has become fixed or inevitable against the majority of the Quraysh due to their persistent stubbornness and rejection of the Prophet's message. It underscores the transition from mere invitation to the certainty of divine retribution for those who, despite clear signs, remain entrenched in disbelief.
